mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses discount rates and increases equity valuation multiples, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE rises by >0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) below their 6-month moving averages indicate contraction in consumer spending and economic activity, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and GDPC1 fails to predict negative returns when the correlation between the series drops below 0.7 in a rolling 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 230), a federal funds rate increase above 0.5% per annum signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces real equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 230 and FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline below 100 relative to the prior month indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained non-farm payrolls growth exceeding 100,000 thousand persons per month indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts decline below 850 thousand units signals reduced consumer confidence in the housing sector, dampening overall economic activity and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when HOUST falls below 850.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), a simultaneous decline in employment growth below 100,000 thousand persons per month indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5 and PAYEMS growth < 100,000.
